Toxic alcohols—primarily **methanol**, **ethylene glycol** , and **isopropanol** —are broken down mainly by **alcohol dehydrogenase (ADH)** and **aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH)** , with organ damage driven largely by their metabolic byproducts rather than the parent alcohols themselves.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXIY355ue_gP7EjBrPEvV2BFQ_VhLz-_JepV8Z8iX2TwqIqTErZc1rn09NP8xqUc0L-LwPUFOmrSGanH4UwHbR37cj4HDyj2zc4UuXc61McOUswmMEz6PSgAcvPWKNBB55Fe4rEeihzboa)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbwHEIkXX1mPlUnya6mFB8PUppOYooN4d6YpQN4Vf9QbtZWUHJ_bXKQP1GCLN_PF33D9WtdpQlC8d6tJoHppMMLIbUzShsNAsuyPKbYmj1fg0MnxKRT0-_eEqPDTRI9E6boDGAegYD5Qdyeq9iEEyjA)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlwEBxCJF1zrcZNSqa4ZSv-w-h_454tLSOFFSbxXVWMU8UwtAQZz0oIsvxN7RaqQc58CBskn5myOUJNnosP2XHpoI1zElxO6MVL9prQkTNjPcKxbSBAUNFL1G_Eel22vLsnYe5PMFAT4OZ9UJKSy7WLjiriycTZoqU651wVu2wLjXiL6mBAW_HS7MKFIwoevv7XzPU3egWFzi)

### Pathway & Toxic Metabolites

- **Methanol:** Oxidized by ADH to formaldehyde and then ALDH to **formic acid** . Formic acid drives severe high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis and damages the optic nerve (causing visual disturbances) and basal ganglia.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESXgHEIkXXMLDqpYeenAZ1PyprTpghJTOGOepoHas4CphkrUd-tDyeiTo0uZtjc4h1gwm-eNgmPHqKJtMD195ZyYSvetP-cMg95Dahhj-0PyHSO-vCaTRpsnZbVkR3R_k)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlwEBxCJF1zrcZNSqa4ZSv-w-h_454tLSOFFSbxXVWMU8UwtAQZz0oIsvxN7RaqQc58CBskn5myOUJNnosP2XHpoI1zElxO6MVL9prQkTNjPcKxbSBAUNFL1G_Eel22vLsnYe5PMFAT4OZ9UJKSy7WLjiriycTZoqU651wVu2wLjXiL6mBAW_HS7MKFIwoevv7XzPU3egWFzi)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXIY355ue_gP7EjBrPEvV2BFQ_VhLz-_JepV8Z8iX2TwqIqTErZc1rn09NP8xqUc0L-LwPUFOmrSGanH4UwHbR37cj4HDyj2zc4UuXc61McOUswmMEz6PSgAcvPWKNBB55Fe4rEeihzboa)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScwHEIkXXIkR2rG5-NQGqvGHaDB00m55X7FhanyGdFSnfu3wYNzYhL_ejKaJsOYlFkPNbSoiXaZz39tyGR0IUMq7QLe6KfS2Ip46HG11ljjqliSCIimjpHkkDyVSpMG4sXvXxMrTf0rnUhwRgNzjUJUBCxik)
- **Ethylene glycol:** Metabolized sequentially into **glycolic acid** and **oxalic acid** . Glycolic acid is the main driver of metabolic acidosis, while oxalic acid binds calcium to form **calcium oxalate crystals** that precipitate in renal tubules, causing acute kidney injury.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbwHEIkXX1mPlUnya6mFB8PUppOYooN4d6YpQN4Vf9QbtZWUHJ_bXKQP1GCLN_PF33D9WtdpQlC8d6tJoHppMMLIbUzShsNAsuyPKbYmj1fg0MnxKRT0-_eEqPDTRI9E6boDGAegYD5Qdyeq9iEEyjA)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlwEBxCJF1zrcZNSqa4ZSv-w-h_454tLSOFFSbxXVWMU8UwtAQZz0oIsvxN7RaqQc58CBskn5myOUJNnosP2XHpoI1zElxO6MVL9prQkTNjPcKxbSBAUNFL1G_Eel22vLsnYe5PMFAT4OZ9UJKSy7WLjiriycTZoqU651wVu2wLjXiL6mBAW_HS7MKFIwoevv7XzPU3egWFzi)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESXgHEIkXXMLDqpYeenAZ1PyprTpghJTOGOepoHas4CphkrUd-tDyeiTo0uZtjc4h1gwm-eNgmPHqKJtMD195ZyYSvetP-cMg95Dahhj-0PyHSO-vCaTRpsnZbVkR3R_k)
- **Isopropanol:** Oxidized by ADH to **acetone** . Unlike methanol and ethylene glycol, isopropanol causes ketosis and central nervous system/gastrointestinal depression **without** causing a high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZwHEIkXXDdOlciJfST1SY0BBGNburBcppbW5fFEEK7ayAdI8KxacZqrcZf8YFr7zZ9OLtzxN2np24Wo_ptiRkzN066Flut7mAJq_AB0-JPMTBzJpAQJ4aJu349sfByuEWtnclUMM_6Q)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXIY355ue_gP7EjBrPEvV2BFQ_VhLz-_JepV8Z8iX2TwqIqTErZc1rn09NP8xqUc0L-LwPUFOmrSGanH4UwHbR37cj4HDyj2zc4UuXc61McOUswmMEz6PSgAcvPWKNBB55Fe4rEeihzboa)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-5ybNEBjEbA&t=17)

### Time Course & Lab Patterns

- **Early stage:** Unmetabolized parent alcohols raise the **osmol gap** , while the **anion gap** may still be normal because toxic organic acids have not yet accumulated.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfAHEIkXXiYStLSkas4OHp9oWlVAQo77p0HeQEKeb6bOQLAw4TARk4dlqJE9zlmecBx-zdIUcaThW9oraJ-5XxkcU76K8Qp6TZ5qZlt0jkRrDOab6rIyV1ogMvu6TYoaHBPamHsTCfdhAt1Zbvp9d-ONGMbPpz7PPwFN5xcw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXIY355ue_gP7EjBrPEvV2BFQ_VhLz-_JepV8Z8iX2TwqIqTErZc1rn09NP8xqUc0L-LwPUFOmrSGanH4UwHbR37cj4HDyj2zc4UuXc61McOUswmMEz6PSgAcvPWKNBB55Fe4rEeihzboa)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbwHEIkXX1mPlUnya6mFB8PUppOYooN4d6YpQN4Vf9QbtZWUHJ_bXKQP1GCLN_PF33D9WtdpQlC8d6tJoHppMMLIbUzShsNAsuyPKbYmj1fg0MnxKRT0-_eEqPDTRI9E6boDGAegYD5Qdyeq9iEEyjA)
- **Later stage:** As parent alcohols are converted into organic acids (for methanol and ethylene glycol), the **osmol gap** falls while a **high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis** rises.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXIY355ue_gP7EjBrPEvV2BFQ_VhLz-_JepV8Z8iX2TwqIqTErZc1rn09NP8xqUc0L-LwPUFOmrSGanH4UwHbR37cj4HDyj2zc4UuXc61McOUswmMEz6PSgAcvPWKNBB55Fe4rEeihzboa)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfAHEIkXXiYStLSkas4OHp9oWlVAQo77p0HeQEKeb6bOQLAw4TARk4dlqJE9zlmecBx-zdIUcaThW9oraJ-5XxkcU76K8Qp6TZ5qZlt0jkRrDOab6rIyV1ogMvu6TYoaHBPamHsTCfdhAt1Zbvp9d-ONGMbPpz7PPwFN5xcw)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbwHEIkXX1mPlUnya6mFB8PUppOYooN4d6YpQN4Vf9QbtZWUHJ_bXKQP1GCLN_PF33D9WtdpQlC8d6tJoHppMMLIbUzShsNAsuyPKbYmj1fg0MnxKRT0-_eEqPDTRI9E6boDGAegYD5Qdyeq9iEEyjA)

### Treatment Principles

- **ADH blockade:** **Fomepizole** (or **ethanol** ) competes with or inhibits ADH, slowing the formation of toxic metabolites from methanol and ethylene glycol so the body can clear the parent compounds more safely.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScwHEIkXXIkR2rG5-NQGqvGHaDB00m55X7FhanyGdFSnfu3wYNzYhL_ejKaJsOYlFkPNbSoiXaZz39tyGR0IUMq7QLe6KfS2Ip46HG11ljjqliSCIimjpHkkDyVSpMG4sXvXxMrTf0rnUhwRgNzjUJUBCxik)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESXgHEIkXXMLDqpYeenAZ1PyprTpghJTOGOepoHas4CphkrUd-tDyeiTo0uZtjc4h1gwm-eNgmPHqKJtMD195ZyYSvetP-cMg95Dahhj-0PyHSO-vCaTRpsnZbVkR3R_k)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeQHEIkXXymxvyWN-PQTsu2hS3JrqtSmaxcRyuUAGSxiW6RUJwcn8axvZNF2Se2PisH3A0dKZP-RGWzbcw6SAg52nh-u4Ev9YYJCOXmEDGcRPZGqXAK9uyDDAPrQao3lJXI4Ttxg0m5OEFvKc1Y5cV-Vt9MW_bH_eqk4)
- **Cofactors & dialysis:** Cofactors such as **folinic/folic acid** (for methanol) or **thiamine/pyridoxine** (for ethylene glycol) support metabolic clearance, while **hemodialysis** removes toxic metabolites, parent alcohols, and severe acid-base or end-organ complications.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlwEBxCJF1zrcZNSqa4ZSv-w-h_454tLSOFFSbxXVWMU8UwtAQZz0oIsvxN7RaqQc58CBskn5myOUJNnosP2XHpoI1zElxO6MVL9prQkTNjPcKxbSBAUNFL1G_Eel22vLsnYe5PMFAT4OZ9UJKSy7WLjiriycTZoqU651wVu2wLjXiL6mBAW_HS7MKFIwoevv7XzPU3egWFzi)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESXgHEIkXXMLDqpYeenAZ1PyprTpghJTOGOepoHas4CphkrUd-tDyeiTo0uZtjc4h1gwm-eNgmPHqKJtMD195ZyYSvetP-cMg95Dahhj-0PyHSO-vCaTRpsnZbVkR3R_k)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZwHEIkXXDdOlciJfST1SY0BBGNburBcppbW5fFEEK7ayAdI8KxacZqrcZf8YFr7zZ9OLtzxN2np24Wo_ptiRkzN066Flut7mAJq_AB0-JPMTBzJpAQJ4aJu349sfByuEWtnclUMM_6Q)[[4]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-5ybNEBjEbA&t=17)

For a deeper clinical breakdown of diagnosis and management, see The Diagnosis and Management of Toxic Alcohol Poisoning in the Emergency Department.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXIY355ue_gP7EjBrPEvV2BFQ_VhLz-_JepV8Z8iX2TwqIqTErZc1rn09NP8xqUc0L-LwPUFOmrSGanH4UwHbR37cj4HDyj2zc4UuXc61McOUswmMEz6PSgAcvPWKNBB55Fe4rEeihzboa)Would you like to explore a **specific toxic alcohol** (methanol, ethylene glycol, or isopropanol), **lab interpretation** (osmol gap vs. anion gap), or **treatment mechanisms** (such as fomepizole and hemodialysis)?

Cofactors & dialysis: Cofactors such as folinic/folic acid (for methanol) or thiamine/pyridoxine (for ethylene glycol) support metabolic clearance, while hemodialysis removes toxic metabolites, parent alcohols, and severe acid-base or end-organ complications.
